kind: a codebase with several teams in it
one_line: Nine engineers, one repository, and a scheduler nobody wants to own.
insider_rationale: wrote it, carries the pager for it
monitor_rationale: opens issues off failing runs; four months, then we look again

ladder.label: api-compat
ladder.text: A published endpoint keeps its shape until every caller has moved.

shared.label: second-eyes
shared.text: Nothing lands on main without a second pair of eyes.

access.label: read-everything
access.text: Every engineer can read and build every part of this repository.

inner_a.label: sched-deterministic
inner_a.text: The scheduler's ordering is deterministic given the same queue.

inner_b.label: sched-no-clock
inner_b.text: The scheduler never reads the wall clock outside one injected source.

clash_a.label: no-flaky-skips
clash_a.text: A failing test is fixed or deleted, never skipped.

clash_b.label: green-main
clash_b.text: Main is green, so that a red build always means the change under it.

extra.label: commit-subject
extra.text: A commit subject says what changed, not which ticket asked for it.

policy.root: One reasoned objection stops a change. Amending something ranked a principle takes the group. Anything we cannot roll back is not decided by silence.
policy.inner: Whoever carries the pager for the scheduler decides the scheduler.
policy.unheld: Infrastructure is decided by whoever holds it.
policy.ladder: Break a published endpoint once and a reviewer signs it off. Twice and the group does. Three times and the answer is no.
policy.inner_amended: Two of us have to object before a scheduler change stops.
policy.middle: Whoever maintains the engine decides the engine.

inner_proposal.text: sort the ready queue by deadline instead of by arrival
inner_proposal.because: arrival order is deterministic but it is not the order anybody wants

inner_objection: deadline order is deterministic only while every task has a deadline, and half of them do not

unheld_proposal.text: move the build cache onto the new object store

monitor_watch.about: the v2 rollout renamed a response field
monitor_watch.because: two callers in this repository still read the old field name
monitor_watch.dismissal: these two do not really conflict

ladder_subject.first: rename the `owner` field on the task body
ladder_subject.second: drop the `retries` field from the run body
ladder_subject.third: change `status` from a string to an enum on the queue body
ladder_subject.because: a caller that has not moved yet reads the old shape and gets nothing
ladder_subject.ruling_1: shipped behind a reader shim and we left it there
ladder_subject.ruling_2: the group agreed one more, then no more

other_subject.text: make the queue name a required key with no default

clash.about: a test that fails once a fortnight
clash.text: skip the timing-sensitive scheduler test until the clock injection lands
clash.because_a: a skipped test is a test that will never be fixed and everybody knows it
clash.because_b: a fortnightly red main teaches everyone to ignore a red main, which costs more
clash.carried: the clock injection is written and behind review; carrying this is cheaper than either horn for exactly as long as that review takes

amend_convention.text: allow a bare ticket reference as a commit subject
amend_convention.because: the ticket says more than any one line could and it is one click away

amend_principle.text: allow a skip when it carries a dated comment and an owner
amend_principle.because: a dated skip with a name on it is checkable, and a deleted test is not

irreversible.text: delete the v1 scheduler and the migration path with it

silence.rationale: every rule anyone proposed would have been worse than the judgement people already exercise, and a line count would be gamed the week it landed
silence.proposal: require a doc comment on every public item

panel.rationale: three people to look at the skip rule for a month
